caption:
Nvidia held 34% of China's data center AI chip market in the first half of 2026, per an IDC report seen by Reuters.
Huawei is right behind at 28%, and Nvidia's shipments there fell 44%.
US export limits and Beijing's push for homegrown chips are reshaping the market.

Can anyone outside China stop Huawei's rise?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechNode

slides.headline: Nvidia's China lead is shrinking fast: Huawei is now just *6 points behind*

slides.heading: 34% vs *28%*
paras: Nvidia held 34% of China's data center AI chip market from January to June 2026, according to an IDC report seen by Reuters.
Huawei took 28%, leaving the gap at just six points.

slides.heading: Nvidia shipments *down 44%*
paras: Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators in China in the first half, down 44% from a year earlier.
Huawei shipped 572,000, up from just over 300,000 in the same period last year.

slides.heading: China builds *its own chips*
paras: Nine of the 11 Chinese chipmakers tracked by IDC grew shipments. Alibaba's T-Head reached 7%, Cambricon 5%, Baidu's Kunlunxin 4% and Hygon 3%.
Non-GPU accelerators jumped nearly 80% to 1.016 million units, while GPU shipments fell 26%.

slides.heading: Why Nvidia is *losing ground*
paras: US export restrictions have limited Nvidia's supply, while Beijing pushes homegrown chips and requires approval to import certain Nvidia models.

paras.t: Jensen Huang has said export controls handed part of China's roughly $50 billion AI chip market to rivals like Huawei.

slides.hook: IDC expects GPU shipments in China to fall again this year. Follow to see if Huawei passes Nvidia next.
